You are at dinner with five friends. The check arrives.

You open Splitwise. You tap Add Expense.

You see: Upgrade to Splitwise Pro to continue.

The free tier now caps you at 3 to 5 expenses per day. With a 10-second ad between each entry. Pro costs $40 a year.

Splitwise was free for 13 years. Then they added a daily expense limit. Then they added ads between transactions. Then they paywalled receipt scanning. Then they pushed Pro at $40 a year forever.

Then a French developer in Montreal shipped Spliit.

Spliit is the free and open source alternative to Splitwise.

His name is Sébastien Castiel. Indie hacker. Next.js instructor. He first built Spliit in 2022 while learning Go. Then he rewrote it in Next.js and made it open source. 75 contributors joined him. The project is translated into dozens of languages on Weblate by volunteers.

No account required. No email. No phone number. No daily limits. No ads.

Here is what it does:

→ Create a group, share one link, your friends are in
→ Add unlimited expenses, every day, forever
→ Split unevenly, by percentage, by share, by exact amount
→ Scan a receipt with your phone and auto-create the expense
→ Attach photos to any expense
→ Categories, search, reimbursements, group balances
→ Multi-currency with live conversion
→ Progressive Web App — works offline on iOS, Android, desktop
→ Use the free hosted version at https://t.co/sZOUhtoRIJ, or one-click deploy your own to Vercel for $0

Here is the wildest part:

Splitwise stores every expense, every photo, every group on their servers. They sold to Plaid in 2024. Tomorrow they could raise Pro to $80. They could add more limits. They could shut the free tier entirely.

Spliit is MIT licensed. Self-host on a Raspberry Pi. Deploy to Vercel free. Your data is in your Postgres. If Sébastien disappears tomorrow, fork the repo and run it forever.

The numbers, today:

2,666 stars. 426 forks. 75 contributors. 25 releases. MIT license. Built since December 2023.

A 13-year-old company charges $40 a year and caps you at 3 expenses a day.

A solo developer in Montreal made it free, unlimited, account-free, and yours.

Your dinners. Your trips. Your splits. No paywall.

Free and self-hosted.
